extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and grants administrators preparing NIH PHS-398 grant applications (PIs, co-PIs, key personnel)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and required-format examples for completing sections of an NIH PHS-398 application, including biographical sketches, cover page human subjects/HESC questions, modular budget fields, personnel justification, and Research Plan attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH format and page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH Provide the following information for the key personnel and other significant contributors in the order listed on Form Page 2. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES. NAME POSITION TITLE eRA COMMONS USER NAME EDUCATION/TRAINING (Begin with baccalaureate or other initial professional education, such as nursing, and include postdoctoral training.) INSTITUTION AND LOCATION DEGREE (if applicable) YEAR(s) FIELD OF STUDY
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page shows the standard biographical sketch sections (A. Personal statement; B. Positions and Honors; C. Selected peer-reviewed publications; D. Research Support). The Personal Statement should summarize the goals of the investigator's work and prior relevant experience and collaborations. Positions and Honors should be listed chronologically. Selected publications are listed (examples provided). Research Support (current and completed) should be listed with grant numbers, project titles, dates, role (e.g., PI), and brief project descriptions. Follow the exact format and do not exceed four pages per person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects / Clinical Trial designation (Cover Page Supplement)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Cover Page Supplement — fields to indicate Human Subjects and Clinical Trial status: 'Human Subjects Clinical Trial?*' and 'Agency-Defined Phase III Clinical Trial?*'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must explicitly indicate whether the proposed project involves human subjects and whether it is a clinical trial (and whether it is an agency-defined Phase III clinical trial). Provide contact information for the applicant organization and the person to be contacted on matters involving the application. These are required form fields on the Cover Page Supplement and must be answered Yes/No as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Embryonic Stem Cells (HESC) reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposed project involve human embryonic stem cells? If the proposed project involves human embryonic stem cells, list below the registration number of the specific cell line(s) from the following list: http://stemcells.nih.gov/research/registry/. Or, if a specific stem cell line cannot be referenced at this time, check the box indicating that one from the registry will be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If HESC are involved, include the registry identifier(s) for the specific cell line(s). If a specific line is not yet selected, indicate that a line from the NIH registry will be used. This is a required compliance field on the Cover Page Supplement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Modular Budget required fields and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Modular Budget forms require per-period budget entries: Start Date, End Date, Budget Period, Direct Cost less Consortium F&AA, Direct Costs, Indirect Costs, Consortium F&A, Total Direct Costs, Indirect Cost Type, Indirect Cost Rate (%), Indirect Cost Base ($), Funds Requested ($), Cognizant Agency (Agency Name, POC Name and Phone Number), Indirect Cost Rate Agreement Date, Total Indirect Costs. Cumulative budget information and budget justifications are also required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each budget period supply the specified fields. Indirect cost documentation must include the cognizant agency and the date of the indirect cost rate agreement. Provide cumulative totals for the entire project period (Section A, B, C totals). Attach Budget Justifications (Personnel Justification, Consortium Justification, Additional Narrative Justification) and include attachments where indicated. Follow the modular budget structure and report funds requested per module/period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan Attachments (required sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHS 398 Research Plan — required attachments/sections to be provided: 1. Application Type (from SF 424 (R&R) Cover Page); 2. Specific Aims; 3. Research Strategy; 6. Protection of Human Subjects; 7. Inclusion of Women and Minorities; 8. Targeted/Planned Enrollment Table; 9. Inclusion of Children; 10. Vertebrate Animals; 11. Select Agent Research; 12. Multiple PD/PI Leadership Plan; 13. Consortium/Contractual Arrangements; 14. Letters of Support; 15. Resource Sharing Plan(s); 16. Appendix; plus other human subjects sections and progress report publication lists as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach the applicable sections of the Research Plan as indicated. The form lists each numbered attachment and provides upload controls. For resubmissions or revisions include an Introduction to Application. Ensure required human subjects, inclusion, vertebrate animal, consortium, resource sharing, and other compliance sections are present and attached in the order and format requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel Justification content and effort reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel Justification must list each key individual with name, degree, role/title, and committed effort expressed as calendar months and percent effort (e.g., 'Peter Myler, Ph.D., Principal Investigator, 1.2 calendar months/10% effort').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each person provide a short statement of responsibilities and relevant expertise. Example entries show PI responsibilities (supervision, oversight, manuscript preparation, grant reporting), staff scientists' duties (experimental design, supervision, animal work), and technicians' duties (specific laboratory tasks). Include benefits calculation (e.g., benefits calculated at X% of base salary with citation to institutional agreement date). If using institutional cores (e.g., Bioinformatics Core), justify core use, list anticipated effort/cost (e.g., equivalent calendar months per year), and describe how core services (pipelines, staff) will support the project and data sharing (e.g., TriTrypDB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims (required Research Plan component; example of expected content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims — a concise statement of the problem background, hypothesis, and the concrete aims to be undertaken (example text presents background on trypanosomatid gene expression, the hypothesis that translational controls tune protein levels, and two numbered aims: Aim 1: Establish ribosome protection assay in T. brucei; Aim 2: Identify genes regulated at the level of translation during T. brucei development).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Specific Aims section should state the scientific question/hypothesis, summarize prior relevant findings, and list numbered, testable aims with brief descriptions of approach and expected outcomes/importance. The example shows inclusion of methodological approach (e.g., RNase I footprinting, Illumina NGS, alignment to genome), rationale for chosen models/stages, and the anticipated significance (new tool, mechanism insights, annotation improvements, identification of drug/vaccine targets). Use clear, succinct aims formatted as Aim 1, Aim 2, etc., and link them to methods and expected impact.
